research_question: Does Henry Hub listed-contract volatility exhibit the Samuelson maturity effect, including the literature-reported winter dependence?
search_scope: Fresh Programme 002 literature inventory only; no legacy internal outcomes or magnitudes used.

sources.title: Weather, storage, and natural gas price dynamics: fundamentals and volatility
Asymmetric impacts of fundamentals on the natural gas futures volatility

claim_map.claim: Nearer natural-gas futures maturities are more volatile than farther maturities.
The time-to-maturity volatility effect is season-dependent and is reported in winter in the Ergen-Rizvanoghlu specification.

expected_observations: Mean absolute same-contract log return decreases in the predeclared order as DTE increases.
The Samuelson contrast is present in winter-withdrawal months and is not stronger in the opposite direction outside winter.
disconfirming_observations: The ordered DTE contrast is flat or opposite under informative power.
Any apparent maturity effect depends on cross-contract returns or on price-conditioned liquidity filtering.
The winter interaction is opposite the literature-reported seasonal pattern without a source-fidelity explanation.
